dialogue.content: こんばんは。今日は宜しくお願いします。時間になりましたら、私の方から、始めますね。
dialogue.English: Good evening. Thank you for coming today. When it's time, I'll start us off.

dialogue.content: こんばんは。相談員です。本日はご相談に来てくださってありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Good evening. I'm the counselor. Thank you for coming in today.

dialogue.content: 最初に年代と性別を教えていただけますか?
dialogue.English: To start, could you please tell me your age group and gender?

dialogue.content: こんばんは、電波が繋がらなくなってしまいました。すいません、宜しくお願いします
dialogue.English: Good evening. I'm sorry, my connection dropped. Thank you for your patience.

dialogue.content: 30代、女性です
dialogue.English: I'm a woman in my 30s.

dialogue.content: 宜しくお願い致します。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I look forward to speaking with you.

dialogue.content: 今日はどのようなご相談ですか?
dialogue.English: What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: はい、子どもの様子がおかしくて
dialogue.English: Yes, my child has been acting strangely...

dialogue.content: それは、ご心配ですね。
dialogue.English: That must be worrying for you.

dialogue.content: 少し詳しくお話していただけますか?
dialogue.English: Could you tell me a bit more about it?

dialogue.content: はい、学校から帰って来たと思ったら部屋で泣いて、声をかけても関係ない❗️って言われて
dialogue.English: Yes. They'll come home from school, and I'll find them crying in their room. When I try to talk to them, they say, "It's none of your business!"

dialogue.content: そんなことがあったんですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So that's what's been happening.

dialogue.content: 戸惑いますね。
dialogue.English: That must be confusing.

dialogue.content: イライラして、大きな声をあげたり
dialogue.English: They get irritated and raise their voice...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ええ、大きな声の後は?
dialogue.English: I see. And what happens after they raise their voice?

dialogue.content: 普通にする時間もあるんです
dialogue.English: There are also times when they act normally.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: その変化は、時間単位ですか?それとも、日にち単位ですか?
dialogue.English: Do these changes happen on an hourly basis? Or is it more day-to-day?

dialogue.content: 時間単位です
dialogue.English: It's on an hourly basis.

dialogue.content: そうですか。それは、どうなっているんだろう、とおろおろしますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. That must make you feel anxious, wondering what's going on.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ちなみにお子さんの年齢はおいくつですか?
dialogue.English: By the way, how old is your child?

dialogue.content: 13才です。
dialogue.English: They're 13 years old.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: たぶん、いじめられているんじゃないかと
dialogue.English: I think they might be being bullied.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。学校での出来事のように思われるんですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So you think it's something happening at school.

dialogue.content: たぶん
dialogue.English: Probably.

dialogue.content: 何か思い当たることがおありですか?
dialogue.English: Is there anything in particular that comes to mind?

dialogue.content: 幼馴染みや私の知っている子どもではないように思うんです
dialogue.English: I don't think it's their childhood friends or any of the children I know.

dialogue.content: そのように感じておられるんですね。知らないお子さんが相手だと余計に、心配になりますね。
dialogue.English: I see, so that's how you feel. It must be even more worrying when it's children you don't know.

dialogue.content: はい、入学半年でバレー部の部活も辞めてしまったので、
dialogue.English: Yes, they also quit the volleyball club six months after starting school, so...

dialogue.content: そうですか。ということは、13歳・・・中学1年生ですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So at 13... that would be the first year of junior high school.

dialogue.content: それからのお友達関係が把握できなくなってしまいました
dialogue.English: Since then, I haven't been able to keep track of their friendships.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: なるほどです。
dialogue.English: I understand.

dialogue.content: 部活を辞めるまでは、お友達関係も把握できていたということですね。
dialogue.English: So, you were able to keep track of their friendships up until they quit the club, is that right?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: お友達がつかめなくなると不安ですよね。
dialogue.English: It's unsettling when you can no longer get a sense of who their friends are.

dialogue.content: 今まではどのような形でお友達のことをつかんでらっしゃったんですか?
dialogue.English: How did you usually keep track of their friends before this?

dialogue.content: 小学校から一緒の子が部活に居たので、自然にわかる感じでした
dialogue.English: There were kids from their elementary school in the club, so I naturally had a sense of things.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so that's how it was.

dialogue.content: お子さんは、どうして部活を辞められたのですか?
dialogue.English: Why did your child quit the club?

dialogue.content: コロナの休校で、ほとんど活動しないのが続き、つまらなくなってです
dialogue.English: Because of the school closures due to COVID, they hardly had any activities, and they said it became boring.

dialogue.content: そうでしたか。コロナで十分活動できなくて可哀想でしたね。
dialogue.English: I see. It's a shame they couldn't do many activities because of COVID.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: お子さんとは、それについてお話されましたか?
dialogue.English: Have you talked with your child about that?

dialogue.content: 部活をやめる事ですか？
dialogue.English: About quitting the club?

dialogue.content: ええ。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: はい、話しました。
dialogue.English: Yes, we talked about it.

dialogue.content: どのようなお話でしたか?
dialogue.English: What was that conversation like?

dialogue.content: その時間を塾に行く事にしました
dialogue.English: We decided they would use that time to go to cram school instead.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so that's what happened.

dialogue.content: 直接お子さんからやめる理由は聞かれましたか?
dialogue.English: Did you hear the reason for quitting directly from your child?

dialogue.content: はい、活動しないので入ってるいみがないと
dialogue.English: Yes, they said there was no point in being in it since there were no activities.

dialogue.content: そうですか。しっかりしたお子さんですね。
dialogue.English: I see. Your child sounds very level-headed.

dialogue.content: 塾に行くのもお子さんの希望でしたか?
dialogue.English: Was it your child's idea to go to cram school as well?

dialogue.content: そこはただ、つまらなくなったって事だとおもいました
dialogue.English: At the time, I just thought that they had gotten bored with it.

dialogue.content: 塾は私が勧めました
dialogue.English: I was the one who suggested cram school.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。お子さんは塾に行かれて何かおっしゃってますか?
dialogue.English: I see. Has your child said anything about going to cram school?

dialogue.content: 中学校が分かれてしまった小学校の同級生に会ったと、言ってました
dialogue.English: They mentioned that they met up with some of their former elementary school classmates who went to different junior high schools.

dialogue.content: 久しぶりに会ったんですね。
dialogue.English: So they saw them after a long time.

dialogue.content: 塾は休まずに通われていますか?
dialogue.English: Are they attending cram school without missing any sessions?

dialogue.content: 私立に進学した子達なので、うちの子より行動範囲が広いんです
dialogue.English: They're kids who went on to private schools, so their circle of activity is wider than my child's.

dialogue.content: 小学校のお友達のことですね。
dialogue.English: You're talking about their friends from elementary school.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 先ほど、お子さんの様子がおかしい原因として、いじめではないか、と言われていましたが、そう思われるのはどうしてですか?
dialogue.English: Earlier, you mentioned you were worried that bullying might be the reason for your child's behavior. What leads you to think that?

dialogue.content: 何となくうちの子がいじめられていると言うより、仲間に引き込まれているようなきがします
dialogue.English: Somehow, rather than my child being bullied, I feel like they're being drawn into a group.

dialogue.content: それで、いじめに加担しているから私にも言えないんじゃないかと
dialogue.English: And I'm worried they might be taking part in bullying, and that's why they can't tell me.

dialogue.content: そう思われると心配ですよね。
dialogue.English: That must be worrying to think about.

dialogue.content: いじめられていたら、物が無くなったりとかありそうですよね
dialogue.English: If they were being bullied, things like their belongings going missing might happen, right?

dialogue.content: そういうこともあるかもしれないですね。
dialogue.English: That could be a possibility, yes.

dialogue.content: お話しているうちに、本人がいじめられてたら、言える気がしてきました
dialogue.English: As we've been talking, I'm starting to feel that if they were the one being bullied, they would be able to tell me.

dialogue.content: そんな風に思われるんですね。
dialogue.English: So that's how you're starting to feel.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: お子さんのことはお母さんが一番よくわかっていらっしゃるから、そうかもしれないですね。
dialogue.English: A mother knows her child best, so that may very well be the case.

dialogue.content: 13歳というと
dialogue.English: At 13 years old...

dialogue.content: 正に思春期ですね。
dialogue.English: that's right in the middle of adolescence.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: お子さんが大人から自立していく過程で、
dialogue.English: In the process of children becoming independent from adults,

dialogue.content: 今まで素直だったのに、反抗的になったり、
dialogue.English: a child who was once obedient might become rebellious,

dialogue.content: かと思えば、甘えてきたりする疾風怒涛の時期と言われています。
dialogue.English: and then at other times, become clingy. It's often called a period of 'storm and stress.'

dialogue.content: いじめに加担していたらどうしたら良いのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: What should I do if they are participating in bullying?

dialogue.content: ご心配なのですね。
dialogue.English: You're very worried about that.

dialogue.content: 反抗的と言うよりは、混乱しているようにおもうので
dialogue.English: Because rather than being rebellious, they seem more confused to me.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 泣いたり、大きな声をあげたり
dialogue.English: The crying and raising their voice...

dialogue.content: 尋常ではないので、いじめられている、ことより、加担しているのではないか、ということの方が心配になっておられるんですね。
dialogue.English: So, because their behavior is so unusual, you've become more worried that they might be participating in bullying, rather than being bullied themselves.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 小さい頃からお子さんを見てこられて、
dialogue.English: Having watched your child since they were little,

dialogue.content: 学校に言った方がいいでしょうか
dialogue.English: Should I talk to the school?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そのようなことになそうなところがおありですか?
dialogue.English: Is there anything about them that makes you think they would do something like that?

dialogue.content: すみません。そのようなことになりそうな・・・です。
dialogue.English: I'm sorry, I meant to ask if there's anything about them that would make that seem likely.

dialogue.content: これまでは普通に友達と仲良くしたり、喧嘩したりで、大した問題は無かったです
dialogue.English: Up until now, they've had normal friendships, getting along and sometimes fighting, but there have been no major problems.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 今回に限っては、あまりにいつもと違うので疑ってしまうんですね。
dialogue.English: But this time, it's so different from their usual self that you're starting to have these suspicions.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 今までのお話をお聴きして
dialogue.English: Listening to what you've said so far,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: あなたはお子さんのことを、本当に愛しく大切に育ててこられたことが伝わってきました。
dialogue.English: it's clear to me that you have raised your child with a great deal of love and care.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 今は、コロナの影響もあって、普段考えもつかないようなことが起こりそうな気がするのも無理のないことだと思います。
dialogue.English: And right now, with the influence of COVID, it's understandable to feel that things you'd never normally imagine might happen.

dialogue.content: お子さんが落ち着かれたときに、学校の話や、塾の話、お友達のお話など無理のないところから
dialogue.English: When your child is calm, maybe you could start with some low-pressure topics, like school, cram school, or their friends,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 少しお話してみられるのは如何でしょうか?
dialogue.English: how about trying to talk with them a little?

dialogue.content: はい、今までいじめられているんじゃないかとばかり考えていたから、何となく納得いきました。話せそうです
dialogue.English: Yes, I was so focused on the idea that they were being bullied, but this makes more sense somehow. I think I can talk to them.

dialogue.content: それは、良かったです。
dialogue.English: I'm glad to hear that.

dialogue.content: 思春期は一般的に情緒が不安定になる時です。
dialogue.English: Adolescence is generally a time of emotional instability.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ホルモンのバランスからいうと、更年期の時くらいに、大きな変化があると言われています。
dialogue.English: In terms of hormonal balance, the changes are said to be as significant as those during menopause.

dialogue.content: お話できれば、あなたも、少し安心されるのではないかと思います。
dialogue.English: If you're able to talk with them, I think you might feel a little more at ease yourself.

dialogue.content: はい、やってみます！
dialogue.English: Yes, I'll give it a try!

dialogue.content: お話されてみてどうだったか、また、お困りのことがあればぜ
dialogue.English: Please let me know how the conversation goes, and if you have any other concerns,

dialogue.content: お力になりたいので、是非、お話にいらしてください。
dialogue.English: I want to help, so please don't hesitate to come and talk with me again.

dialogue.content: また相談に来ます！ありがとうございました！
dialogue.English: I'll come back to talk again! Thank you very much!

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you as well.

dialogue.content: では、本日の相談を終了致しますね。
dialogue.English: Alright, we will now conclude today's session.

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you very much.

dialogue.content: （失礼します）
dialogue.English: (Goodbye.)

dialogue.content: ロールプレイを終了しますね。
dialogue.English: We will now end the role-play.
